events.description: Flagship Event: A competitive event featuring OA (Online Assessment) and interview-based questions across all three domains, designed to test participants’ technical knowledge, problem-solving abilities, and interview readiness.
rules:
Round 1: Online Assessment – Separate for each domain
-Hardware:- Questions based on core electrical and electronics subjects.
-Software:- Questions based on programming and technical concepts.
- Consultancy:- Questions on logical reasoning, aptitude, data analysis, and basic graphical interpretation.
Round 2: Interview + Group Discussion (GD) – Evaluates technical knowledge, communication skills, and teamwork. It is necessary for shortlisted students to take part in the interview.

events.description: A competitive technical event featuring Web Development and Machine Learning (ML) based Problem Statements (PS), challenging participants to apply their technical knowledge, creativity, and problem-solving skills.
rules: Eligibility: B.Tech students from all branches are eligible to participate.
Team Formation: Teams must consist of 1–4 members from the same academic year. Inter-year teams are not allowed.
Problem Statement: The problem statement (PS) will be released one week before the commencement of Avishkar.
Mid-Evaluation: Mid-evaluation will be conducted three days after the problem statement is released.
Originality: Projects must be original student work. Plagiarism is strictly prohibited.
Project Demonstration: Teams must present a working prototype, functional application, or live demo.
Resources: Participants must arrange their own laptops and other required resources.
Evaluation Criteria: Projects will be judged on innovation, technical implementation, feasibility, and presentation.

events.description: A competitive programming (CP) event designed to test participants' coding skills, logical reasoning, and algorithmic problem-solving abilities.
rules: Eligibility: Students from all courses are eligible to participate.
Round 1 – Online Coding Round: Participants will solve programming problems online to test their coding skills and problem-solving abilities.
Round 2 – Offline Coding Round: Shortlisted participants will compete in an offline coding round to evaluate their programming proficiency and logical thinking.
Round 3 – Interview: Finalists will undergo an interview to assess their technical knowledge, coding concepts, and problem-solving approach.
Originality: Participants must submit their own solutions. Plagiarism or any unfair means are strictly prohibited.
Evaluation: Participants will be judged on coding accuracy, efficiency, problem-solving skills, and technical understanding.
Judging: The decision of the judging panel will be final.

events.description: A fun and competitive bidding-based event where participants bid on technical questions they are confident they can answer, combining strategy, knowledge, and quick thinking.
rules: Eligibility: Students from all years and branches are eligible to participate.

Round 1 – Question Bidding: Teams will bid on questions they believe they can answer correctly. The bid amount will be deducted from their points or allotted balance regardless of whether the answer is correct or incorrect.
Round 2 – Mock IPL Auction: Participants will take part in a mock IPL auction, bidding for players and building their teams strategically.
Fair Play: Participants must follow the bidding rules and instructions provided by the organizers.

events.description: A hands-on technical event designed for students interested in core engineering, embedded systems, and hardware development. Participants tackle real-world problem statements and build practical solutions using hardware platforms such as Arduino, sensors, microcontrollers, and other electronic components.
rules: Eligibility: Students from all years are eligible to participate.
Team Size: Each team must consist of 4 members.
Rounds: The event will consist of two rounds: Mid-Evaluation and Final Evaluation. Both rounds will contribute to the final score.
Mid-Evaluation: Teams will present their project progress for evaluation. No PPT presentation is required.
Final Evaluation: Teams must present a PPT explaining their project and demonstrate the working hardware prototype.
Resources: Teams must arrange their own hardware components, tools, and other required resources.
Evaluation Criteria: Projects will be judged on innovation, technical implementation, functionality, and presentation.

events.description: An exciting treasure hunt event that combines fun, creativity, humour, and adventure. Participants begin with an entertaining quiz featuring memes, riddles, quirky challenges, and hilarious questions with unexpected answers. The excitement continues with a treasure hunt across the entire college campus, where participants follow clues, solve puzzles, and race to discover the hidden treasure.
rules: Eligibility: Students from all years and branches are eligible to participate.
Team Formation: Inter-year teams are not allowed; all team members must belong to the same academic year.
Round 1 – Fun Quiz: Challenges may include meme identification, movie guessing, crosswords, song guessing through emojis, and fun trivia.
Bonus Challenges: Bonus-point questions and fun dares will be introduced between Rounds 1 and 2. Teams can choose whether to attempt them and earn additional points.
Round 2 – Audio Round: Participants will identify songs, advertisements, and other audio clips, along with fun trivia challenges.
Round 3 – Treasure Hunt: Participants must follow clues hidden across the college campus to complete the treasure hunt.
Transportation: Bicycles are allowed during the treasure hunt; the use of e-rickshaws is strictly prohibited.
Fair Play: Participants must follow all instructions given by the organizers throughout the event.

events.description: A competitive analytical problem-solving event testing participants’ logical reasoning, mathematical aptitude, probability, and quick decision-making through challenging puzzles and timed rounds.
rules: Eligibility: Students from all years and branches are eligible to participate.
Round 1 – Analytical Quiz: Participants will solve questions based on logical reasoning, mathematical aptitude, probability, and analytical thinking within a given time limit.
Round 2 – Problem-Solving Challenge: Shortlisted participants will tackle challenging puzzles and time-bound problems requiring quick decision-making, logical reasoning, and strategic thinking.
Time Limit: Participants must complete each round within the allotted time.
Fair Play: Any use of unfair means will lead to disqualification.
